question: Which earthquake rescue operation by the National Response force in myanmar in March 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Operation Bramha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Operation Bramha** was a high-stakes humanitarian mission launched by the **Government of India** in **March 2025** to provide immediate relief to **Myanmar** following a devastating **earthquake**.
 
• The **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** spearheaded the mission, deploying multiple specialized teams equipped with **advanced search and rescue tools**, including **canine squads** and **chip-based life detectors**.
 
• The operation focused on the hardest-hit regions of **Myanmar**, where the seismic activity caused extensive damage to infrastructure and residential buildings, requiring **urban search and rescue (USAR)** expertise.
 
• India utilized the **C-17 Globemaster III** aircraft of the **Indian Air Force** to transport over **100 personnel**, along with emergency **medical supplies**, **tents**, and **ready-to-eat meals** to the affected zones.
 
• This mission reinforces India's role as the **"First Responder"** in the **Indian Ocean Region** and its commitment to the **"Neighborhood First"** policy during natural calamities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**:
 
 
• The **NDRF** was constituted in the year **2006** under the **Disaster Management Act, 2005**, specifically for the purpose of specialized response to natural and man-made disasters.
 
• It operates under the **Ministry of Home Affairs** and is headquartered in **New Delhi**, with various battalions stationed across **India** for rapid deployment.
 
 
 
• **India-Myanmar Relations in Disaster Management**:
 
 
• India has a history of assisting **Myanmar**, such as during **Cyclone Mocha** in **2023** under **Operation Karuna**, where **Indian Navy** ships delivered essential relief materials.
 
• The collaboration between the two nations is vital due to their shared **1,643 km long land border** and proximity in the **Bay of Bengal**.
 
 
 
• **Humanitarian Assistance and Disaster Relief (HADR)**:
 
 
• **HADR** operations are a core component of India's **soft power** diplomacy, demonstrating technical capability and regional leadership.
 
• Other notable operations include **Operation Dost** (the **2023 Turkey-Syria earthquake**) and **Operation Maitri** (the **2015 Nepal earthquake**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Seismic Vulnerability**: **Myanmar** is located in a seismically active zone where the **Indian Plate** subducts under the **Burma Microplate**, making it prone to high-magnitude earthquakes.
 
• **Technical Coordination**: The success of **Operation Bramha** relied on the **Ministry of External Affairs (MEA)** coordinating with the **Myanmar** authorities to ensure a seamless "green corridor" for aid delivery.
 
• **Medical Aid**: A significant part of the relief package included **Level-2 and Level-3 medical facilities** capable of performing emergency surgeries in field conditions.
 
• **Global Standards**: **NDRF** teams follow the guidelines of the **International Search and Rescue Advisory Group (INSARAG)**, ensuring that their methods are compatible with international disaster response protocols.
